bounds: Two concurrent calls, three entries, batch size two, one malformed entry, matching/unavailable receipts and bounded cursor revisions. Separate serial reliable-progress case has three invocations.
limitations: Two concurrent adoption calls, three retained entries (two valid and one malformed), a two-entry batch and digest ranks rather than cryptographic strings. The conflict case uses an unmatched receipt to represent provider, event, payload or historical digest conflicts.

The producer is quiescent: current KV push/pop methods reject queue writes. Old deployed producers must be stopped before KV list removal. Without this assumption a stale KV read/modify/write can erase newly appended work; the negative witness demonstrates that excluded behavior.

KV list removal may restore already-adopted entries under concurrent removers. The model allows stale removal snapshots; matching durable SQL receipts prevent reopening completed work. KV eventual visibility and durability are external assumptions, not proved by the local namespace fixture.

The SQL transaction and exact payload/terminal receipt predicates are abstracted as matching, absent or unavailable. PGlite exercises real SQL; PostgreSQL checks actual row-lock waiting and concurrent cursor reservation. The production KV and isolated loopback Redis adapters exercise removal; TypeScript refinement and production provider behavior are not proved.

Cursor reservations advance only selection hints. Losing a cursor reply or a progress CAS cannot authorize removal. The SQL receipt, not cursor position, is required before LREM. Scope includes the configured backend/environment and one legacy queue.

Production limits attempts to 25 per list and uses a separate one-second per-list work budget. The model abstracts this as one or two attempted entries. Full KV-array reads and hashing remain unbounded by the work timer, and a single in-flight SQL or cache call can outlive it.

The serial progress case assumes a fixed three-entry snapshot, available SQL, three fair cron invocations and returning operations. It establishes transfer of the two valid entries despite a permanent poison entry and one-attempt budgets; it does not promise unconditional backlog clearance or resolution of unavailable historical receipts.

Outbox handler effects, Stripe signature verification, billing idempotency and retention are separate protocols. StripeDeliveryOutbox retains its existing lease model; a durable handoff here is not proof of end-to-end external delivery.

Identical raw multiplicity and SHA256 collisions are outside the set abstraction. Actual tests preserve identical copies until a matching receipt and remove them individually; collision resistance is assumed. Unknown or malformed raws remain retained for operator reconciliation with payload-free diagnostics.

assumptions: Each started cursor, SQL and Redis operation eventually returns or fails; weak fairness of Advance is assumed.
Each started cursor, SQL and KV operation eventually returns or fails; weak fairness of Advance is assumed.
Each started operation eventually returns or fails, including explicit unavailable receipt results; weak fairness of Advance is assumed.

One serial cron makes three invocations on a fixed three-entry snapshot with available SQL. Start, First and Finish are weakly fair; no old producer writes, and at least the first reserved entry is attempted.
